title: Segregated control plane failover and adaptive load-shedding for Dedicated & Private
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Dedicated and Private customers running isolated control planes can experience noisy neighbor incidents and upgrade-induced regressions that compromise latency SLOs and customer throughput. We need deterministic multi-region failover, tenant-aware circuit breakers, and adaptive load-shedding that preserves high-priority SLAs during capacity pressure and upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Can automatically failover control-plane API traffic for an affected Dedicated region to a configured secondary region within target RTO (<= 90s) without cross-tenant data leaks
Per-tenant SLO calculations and safety thresholds are available in Console (latency P95, error-rate, tokens/sec) and can be used to trigger tenant isolation
Circuit breaker rules that operate at route/model/tenant granularity exist and trip before cluster-wide overload (configurable thresholds and cooldowns), with observable events in tracing/logs
Adaptive load-shedding policy that degrades best-effort tenants and preserves reserved/priority commitments, with audit logs and billing annotations
Upgrade rollouts to control planes include canary gating based on tenant-level SLOs and automatic automatic rollback criteria
Runbook documented with step-by-step failover, tenant isolation, and post-incident checklist; automated playbook hooks added to PagerDuty run actions
tasks: Design: define multi-region control plane failover state machine, leader election constraints for private VPCs, and data-plane compatibility requirements
Implementation: add tenant-scoped circuit breaker middleware to control plane API gateway (model + route + token buckets)
Implementation: integrate adaptive load-shedding policy into serving runtime (priority tagging, token-based backpressure)
Metrics: add tenant-level SLO metrics export (P50/P95/P99 latency, errors, tokens/sec) to Console and SLI pipelines
Safety: extend upgrade orchestrator with preflight SLO checks and canary percentage ramp steps tied to tenant health
Tests: chaos tests for region outage, noisy tenant saturation, and rolling upgrade scenarios in staging
Docs & Runbook: publish step-by-step incident actions and update customer-facing SLA docs
design_notes: Key decision: prefer control-plane failover using DNS + weighted routing with short TTLs for Dedicated customers (region preference + emergency override flag) to avoid cross-VPC peering complexity. For Private (VPC-on-prem) deployments we will implement an in-band control-plane proxy that can be pointed to a secondary management endpoint under ops control. Circuit breakers will initially be conservative: trip on sustained 5-minute token saturation or 1-minute P95 degradation > 2x baseline.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: failing over control-plane endpoints could cause in-flight token validation errors. Mitigation: pre-create temporary auth tokens and include graceful retry logic in SDKs and gateways
Risk: overzealous load-shedding may impact high-value customers. Mitigation: honor reserved capacity and customer priority metadata; add emergency override and manual un-shed action in Console
Risk: telemetry gaps for Private deployments. Mitigation: lightweight agent for SLI export and an offline sync path for audit logs

2025-02-18 Liam O'Connor: Sketched failover state machine; discovered VPC private endpoints prevent simple DNS switch for some Private installs. Proposing in-band proxy for those customers. Added to design notes.

2025-02-22 Infrastructure review: Dan Rivera: raised concern about auth token invalidation during failover — suggested temporary cross-signing tokens and SDK retry window. Marked as dependency for security review.
2025-02-25 Reliability: Priya Menon: request for tenant-priority metadata surfaced — will add 2 fields (reserved_capacity, business_tier) to tenant config schema. Impact: migration script required.
2025-03-01 Engineering: PR #482 opened for circuit breaker middleware; unit tests added. Waiting on integration tests and security review.

2025-03-03 QA: Added staging chaos test plan covering region outage and noisy-consumer saturation. Early results show circuit breaker trips under expected thresholds; tuning required for cooldown window.
next_steps: Finish integration tests for middleware, complete security review for token cross-signing, run full chaos suite in staging week of 2025-03-10, and schedule incremental rollout in production with canary tenants and manual abort controls.
postmortem_plan: If a production incident occurs after rollout, capture timeline, triage decisions, metrics (tenant SLOs and shed events), and customer impact. Publish postmortem to Confluence and attach action items to this ticket.
